acceptance_criteria: A pull request touching source or tests runs full-regression.
A pull request touching only documentation does not.
Neither the workflow header comment nor the protocol prose still describes the gate as dispatch-only.
The pull request body names the path expressions and walks at least two concrete examples.
tests/test_ci_workflow_fast_pr_regression.py asserts the current topology and passes.

baseline.authority: docs/design/PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_15C_REGRESSION_GATE_RUNS_WHEN_THE_CORE_CHANGES.md (FROZEN, merged 2026-09-15). It narrows the 2026-09-06 DEV.TEST.1 topology rather than reversing it, and fixes the two rules that bound the path expressions.
baseline.observed: full-regression and po-scope-check both report skipping with duration zero on every pull request. PR #359 merged with all checks green while five tests were failing on main, and they stayed failing until a session ran the suite by hand days later. A previous attempt at this movement completed the workflow and prose change and reported three stale dispatch-only assertions in the CI test file that its own packet had placed out of scope; that exclusion was the packet's error and is corrected here.
baseline.what_exists:
gh pr checks 359, verbatim:

  validate         pass       23s
  full-regression  skipping   0
  po-scope-check   skipping   0

The conditions live in .github/workflows/validation.yml. The regression job is gated on the event type:

  full-regression:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch'

and the scope job on the event type and the branch name:

  po-scope-check:
    if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && startsWith(github.head_ref, 'gov/po-')

The file's header comment records the 2026-09-06 reasoning at length, cites docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md under CI validation policy, and names workflow run 34020356372 as one-time proof that parallel execution works on GitHub-hosted infrastructure. That comment is now partly superseded and must be corrected rather than deleted wholesale: the cost reasoning it records still stands and is the reason this movement adds a condition instead of removing one.

invariants: workflow_dispatch continues to work as it does today.
The 2026-09-06 cost reasoning stays recorded. It is superseded in scope, not in substance.
report.merge_gate: The worker opens the pull request and does not merge it.
report.objective: The regression gate runs on a pull request that touches anything the suite can break, and stays off for a documentation-only change.
output_contract: A SESSION CLOSE on the relay as one NEXUS_SESSION_PACKET.

recommended_reasoning.reason: One workflow condition and two pieces of prose, against a record that already fixes the rules. The judgement is in which paths fall on which side, which the packet constrains.

requirements: A path that no rule matches must RUN, not skip. A condition whose default is to skip reproduces the defect this movement exists to remove, in a form that is harder to notice.
A documentation-only exclusion excludes documentation. Excluding a directory because it mostly contains documentation would skip the gate for the source that also lives there.

Verify the condition by reasoning about concrete example paths in the pull request body: name at least one path that runs and one that does not, and for a directory holding both kinds, say which way it falls and why.
risks: The condition is only testable by merging it and watching the next few pull requests. Write it so a wrong guess fails safe -- by running -- rather than by silently skipping.
Deleting the header comment instead of correcting it would erase the reason the gate is conditional, and the next session would read an unconditional gate as an oversight.

in: Make full-regression run on a pull request whose changes touch source, tests, project state, workflows or deployment manifests, and not run on a pull request whose changes touch only documentation and records.
State the exact path expressions in the pull request body, and say for each why it is on the side it is on.

Correct the header comment in .github/workflows/validation.yml and the CI validation policy prose in docs/AI_DEVELOPMENT_PROTOCOL.md so that neither still describes the superseded topology. Keep the cost reasoning; it is why the gate is conditional rather than unconditional.
Report what po-scope-check's condition currently does and whether it is correct. Do not change it: 15C section 5 leaves that open and asks only for the finding.

Update tests/test_ci_workflow_fast_pr_regression.py, which asserts the superseded dispatch-only topology. Those assertions are the enforcement of the policy 15C replaced, so they move with it: assert what the gate does now, and do not simply delete the ones that no longer hold.
out: Running the full suite on every pull request. 15C section 4 records that option and why it was rejected.
Splitting the suite into a fast and a slow half. 15C section 5 leaves that to its own record.
